intro.name: Richard Sepši
intro.shortdesc: I’m a student from Bratislava, Slovakia, interested in 3D graphics and UX/UI Design. I always do my best to create something that both looks nice and works well.

aboutme.title: About me
aboutme.s1text1: I first began to develop my current interests when I was about 9 years old. I used to play games on my phone, and I thought that it would be fun to try making my own, so I signed up for a local game programming course. We developed various simple games in basic programming languages like Dark Basic Pro and App Game Kit, later Python or C++, and we also worked on the games' visuals.
aboutme.s1text2: After some time, I also tried developing 3D games, which I quite enjoyed, but it was much more difficult than the 2D games I worked on previously, even if the game itself was really simple. A big problem with the simple tools and basic programming languages was that there was no way to edit the levels visually, so everything had to be coded manually. I wanted a better solution. After searching for something and asking around, I discovered Unreal Engine. It looked great, so I downloaded it and started experimenting with it. Over time, I learned a lot about real-time 3D visuals used in games, as well as 3D computer graphics in general.
aboutme.s1text3: While I worked on games, I also signed up for a web development course that caught my interest. Initially, we covered HTML and CSS, later we continued with JavaScript and I even tried PHP, React and SCSS. I realized that I enjoy designing websites more than coding, however, I found coding skills useful as well, and I kept working on them. It allowed me to make my own functional websites just like this one.
aboutme.s2text1: Most of the projects I worked on over the recent years were primarily focused on 3D graphics and UX/UI Design, and I also built my portfolio website with that in mind. The majority of them do not perfectly fit under these two categories though. Each project has its own dedicated page containing more details. Coding projects currently do not have a separate category here and they will usually also be listed under graphics. Those that do not involve graphics will only be available on my GitHub. There is a separate photography page, which is currently work in progress and only accessible by search.
aboutme.s2text2: Besides projects for real clients, my portfolio also includes my personal projects that I often work on in my free time. Their primary purpose is learning new skills and software, while also improving in what I already know.
aboutme.s2text3: As a supporter of open source software, I often like to make use of such tools in my projects and I also use Fedora Linux as my primary system. However, I have no problem with using industry standard software as well, which I still work with most of the time.
aboutme.s3text1: Currently I'm looking to focus mainly on 3D graphics and/or UX/UI design, but I'd also like to improve in all of the other areas I mention here on my portfolio, including programming, photography and some other related fields. I realize it's quite a broad range of skills to focus on, but only more experience can allow me to make the correct decision about what I'm going to specialize in and focus my career on. Moreover, making this decision deosn't force me to abandon my other interests.
aboutme.s3text2: Progress in the digital landscape is also as fast as it's ever been, which strongly influences the job market. My skills and portfolio will have to adapt. I'm always open to learning something new and expanding my skillset. If you'd like to find out more about me and my work, feel free to keep looking around and check out the 3D and 2D Graphics pages.
aboutme.s4text1: In my opinion, AI can help increase skilled person's productivity. Having used many of the major AI tools, I believe I understand why and how it is used, however I also believe that to properly learn a skill, more is needed than just getting something done primarily with AI. That's why currently most of the projects on my portfolio, and all of my personal projects are done without the use of AI, exceptions for those being the use of AI for inspiration, occasionally for photo outpainting and text manipulation. If AI was used, it's use will be described on the project's page.

education.title: Education
education.i2title: Prague University of Economics and Business - Multimedia in economic practice

contact.title: Contact me
contact.helptext1: This website is open source and developed on GitHub.
contact.helptext2: If you have found a bug/error or you have an improvement suggestion, don't hesitate to submit a new issue on GitHub.

metrostation.about:
This project is a remake of one of the first personal 3D projects that I worked on. It's supposed to be a newly built metro station in a hypothetical metro in Bratislava.
Everything was modeled in Cinema 4D then texured and rendered in Blender. All of the assets are my own except the floor material, which comes from AmbientCG.

seasidecliffs.about: This is a project I originally started working on to be a replacement for my old banner. Not only did I want to give it a new look, but I also wanted to use only my own assets and learn some things along the way. I feel like it has definitely served that purpouse. I got the idea for the look from a photo of Broken Beach on Bali, I wanted to create something similar. I started with blocking out the scene and then it was just about creating the assets. It unfortunately took a pretty long time as I wanted each asset to be my own and I couldn't work on the project often. I also struggled with my computer not beeing able to keep up with the scene's complexity and I was barely able to make the final render because of my GPUs very limited vram. In spite of all the struggles, I'm glad I made the project as was able to learn a lot and I'll know how to better approach creating such a project in the future. I hope you find it interesting.

natart.about: NatArt is a company that specializes in making various national-themed souvenirs since 2016. Their name combines the words National and Art, as the beauty of nations is the basis for their work. Now they are exapnding online in response to the increasing interest in their products.
natart.mywork: I worked primarily on designing the online store as well as things like invoices and e-mails.

zelenaskola.about:
"Projekty a blog zelenej školy" or "Projects and blog of the green school" is a website for a team of students from the high school that I attended. Their goal is to make the school more green through various projects.
This website is made to present their projects, highlight their goals, as well as to host their blog.
zelenaskola.mywork: I worked on the website's design. It's simple, consisting of just two pages. The bottom right variant was not used (bottom variant if you're on mobile), it's an older version of the blog page.

realizmusnaorave.about:
Realizmus na Orave is a simple audioguide progressive web app made to guide you through most of the major sights from the time of Realism in the Orava region of Slovakia.
The project/app is not currently available as it was never publicly released. However, most of the app's functionality was finished and is ready to be used.
realizmusnaorave.mywork: I worked on the app's UI, the download screen and various other parts of the app including the icons. I also provided some of the photos used in the app, the rest came from different sources.

unageo.desc: Unageo is a modern, open-source, sans-serif typeface that uses perfect geometry and uniform stroke width where possible, but still maintains great readability.
unageo.desc2: Unageo supports hundreds of languages in latin, cyrillic and greek scripts.
unageo.desc3: + Cyrillic and greek scripts, scroll down to find out more!
unageo.otlabel1: Eastern cyrillic forms (к, ю, ж, в, з) "ss01"
unageo.tryplaceholder: Type here to try out unageo and it's variable features
unageo.cyrillic: Unageo cyrillic was made in Bulgarian style. It uses more rounded geometric shapes and letters have more variety in their height, which makes reading easier.
unageo.greek: Unageo greek follows the same style with perfect geometry, but completes it with smooth lines and adds extra geometric features to make it more unique and distinct.
unageo.story1: Over the years, I have used many different fonts for my projects and sometimes I thought that to better match my style, I could try to make my own typeface. I decided to give it a shot, even though I knew almost nothing about font creation itsef. I only knew that I would like my font to be geometric because that's my preferred style.
unageo.story2: I decided to work on the typeface with an unusual workflow. I made the characters in Inkscape, which I'm familiar with. Then I imported the outlines into FontForge, which I only tried for the first time. The process didn't take as long as I expected, and everything was done in a few days. I made each glyph in light and Black variant, made sure they were interpolable and then I adjusted the metrics and added kerning.
unageo.story3: Of course, I ran into some issues along the way and learned that fonts are more complicated than they look like. After I had everything figured out, I used Fontmake to generate a variable fonts and Fonttools to create static instances. There is still a lot I can learn, especially if I decide to make another font, and I'm sure this one isn't perfect either, so if you have an idea for an improvement, don't hesitate to submit a new issue on GitHub, and I'll take a look at it. See further down below.
unageo.ost:
Unageo is an open source typeface developed on GitHub.
If you have an idea for an improvement, bug to report or any other comment/suggestion, feel free to submit a new issue on GitHub.
Latest relase as well as the bleeding edge version is always available on GitHub along with the source files.
Typeface was recently accepted into Google Fonts and should be available in 2026 Q2.

wordgrind.about: WordGrind (言葉作業ゲー) is a simple web app for word memorization. It works by randomly picking a word from a deck and asking for the answer. Besides words and their answers it also features "back sides" (made for english meaning of kanji words) and hints, which can all be fully customized. It's a project that I primarily made for my personal use, however, you can also download it from GitHub and use it freely if you want.

opucestauprchlika.about:
The goal of this project was to transform a paper-based story game by OPU (Organizace pro pomoc uprchlíkům) about the journey of an Ukrainian family fleeing the war into a digital format. Its main purpose is to educate about the challenges these families face, with a particular focus on educating middle school students.
My Role in the Project
I was responsible for designing the game's interface and developing a high-fidelity clickable prototype using Figma, while following the organization's existing visual identity guidelines. In addition, I worked on shortening the texts, to enhance the game's appeal and ensure it fits on smaller screens.

intro.shortdesc: I’m a student from Bratislava, Slovakia, interested in 3D graphics and UX/UI Design. I always do my best to create something that both looks nice and works well.

aboutme.title: About me
aboutme.s1text1: I first began to develop my current interests when I was about 9 years old. I used to play games on my phone, and I thought that it would be fun to try making my own, so I signed up for a local game programming course. We developed various simple games in basic programming languages like Dark Basic Pro and App Game Kit, later Python or C++, and we also worked on the games' visuals.
aboutme.s1text2: After some time, I also tried developing 3D games, which I quite enjoyed, but it was much more difficult than the 2D games I worked on previously, even if the game itself was really simple. A big problem with the simple tools and basic programming languages was that there was no way to edit the levels visually, so everything had to be coded manually. I wanted a better solution. After searching for something and asking around, I discovered Unreal Engine. It looked great, so I downloaded it and started experimenting with it. Over time, I learned a lot about real-time 3D visuals used in games, as well as 3D computer graphics in general.
aboutme.s1text3: While I worked on games, I also signed up for a web development course that caught my interest. Initially, we covered HTML and CSS, later we continued with JavaScript and I even tried PHP, React and SCSS. I realized that I enjoy designing websites more than coding, however, I found coding skills useful as well, and I kept working on them. It allowed me to make my own functional websites just like this one.
aboutme.s2text1: Most of the projects I worked on over the recent years were primarily focused on 3D graphics and UX/UI Design, and I also built my portfolio website with that in mind. The majority of them do not perfectly fit under these two categories though. Each project has its own dedicated page containing more details. Coding projects currently do not have a separate category here and they will usually also be listed under graphics. Those that do not involve graphics will only be available on my GitHub. There is a separate photography page, which is currently work in progress and only accessible by search.
aboutme.s2text2: Besides projects for real clients, my portfolio also includes my personal projects that I often work on in my free time. Their primary purpose is learning new skills and software, while also improving in what I already know.
aboutme.s2text3: As a supporter of open source software, I often like to make use of such tools in my projects and I also use Fedora Linux as my primary system. However, I have no problem with using industry standard software as well, which I still work with most of the time.
aboutme.s3text1: Currently I'm looking to focus mainly on 3D graphics and/or UX/UI design, but I'd also like to improve in all of the other areas I mention here on my portfolio, including programming, photography and some other related fields. I realize it's quite a broad range of skills to focus on, but only more experience can allow me to make the correct decision about what I'm going to specialize in and focus my career on. Moreover, making this decision deosn't force me to abandon my other interests.
aboutme.s3text2: Progress in the digital landscape is also as fast as it's ever been, which strongly influences the job market. My skills and portfolio will have to adapt. I'm always open to learning something new and expanding my skillset. If you'd like to find out more about me and my work, feel free to keep looking around and check out the 3D and 2D Graphics pages.
aboutme.s4text1: In my opinion, AI can help increase skilled person's productivity. Having used many of the major AI tools, I believe I understand why and how it is used, however I also believe that to properly learn a skill, more is needed than just getting something done primarily with AI. That's why currently most of the projects on my portfolio, and all of my personal projects are done without the use of AI, exceptions for those being the use of AI for inspiration, occasionally for photo outpainting and text manipulation. If AI was used, it's use will be described on the project's page.

education.title: Education
education.i2title: Prague University of Economics and Business - Multimedia in economic practice

contact.title: Contact me
contact.helptext1: This website is open source and developed on GitHub.
contact.helptext2: If you have found a bug/error or you have an improvement suggestion, don't hesitate to submit a new issue on GitHub.

metrostation.about:
This project is a remake of one of the first personal 3D projects that I worked on. It's supposed to be a newly built metro station in a hypothetical metro in Bratislava.
Everything was modeled in Cinema 4D then texured and rendered in Blender. All of the assets are my own except the floor material, which comes from AmbientCG.

seasidecliffs.about: This is a project I originally started working on to be a replacement for my old banner. Not only did I want to give it a new look, but I also wanted to use only my own assets and learn some things along the way. I feel like it has definitely served that purpouse. I got the idea for the look from a photo of Broken Beach on Bali, I wanted to create something similar. I started with blocking out the scene and then it was just about creating the assets. It unfortunately took a pretty long time as I wanted each asset to be my own and I couldn't work on the project often. I also struggled with my computer not beeing able to keep up with the scene's complexity and I was barely able to make the final render because of my GPUs very limited vram. In spite of all the struggles, I'm glad I made the project as was able to learn a lot and I'll know how to better approach creating such a project in the future. I hope you find it interesting.

natart.about: NatArt is a company that specializes in making various national-themed souvenirs since 2016. Their name combines the words National and Art, as the beauty of nations is the basis for their work. Now they are exapnding online in response to the increasing interest in their products.
natart.mywork: I worked primarily on designing the online store as well as things like invoices and e-mails.

zelenaskola.about:
"Projekty a blog zelenej školy" or "Projects and blog of the green school" is a website for a team of students from the high school that I attended. Their goal is to make the school more green through various projects.
This website is made to present their projects, highlight their goals, as well as to host their blog.
zelenaskola.mywork: I worked on the website's design. It's simple, consisting of just two pages. The bottom right variant was not used (bottom variant if you're on mobile), it's an older version of the blog page.

realizmusnaorave.about:
Realizmus na Orave is a simple audioguide progressive web app made to guide you through most of the major sights from the time of Realism in the Orava region of Slovakia.
The project/app is not currently available as it was never publicly released. However, most of the app's functionality was finished and is ready to be used.
realizmusnaorave.mywork: I worked on the app's UI, the download screen and various other parts of the app including the icons. I also provided some of the photos used in the app, the rest came from different sources.

unageo.desc: Unageo is a modern, open-source, sans-serif typeface that uses perfect geometry and uniform stroke width where possible, but still maintains great readability.
unageo.desc2: Unageo supports hundreds of languages in latin, cyrillic and greek scripts.
unageo.desc3: + Cyrillic and greek scripts, scroll down to find out more!
unageo.otlabel1: Eastern cyrillic forms (к, ю, ж, в, з) "ss01"
unageo.cyrillic: Unageo cyrillic was made in Bulgarian style. It uses more rounded geometric shapes and letters have more variety in their height, which makes reading easier.
unageo.greek: Unageo greek follows the same style with perfect geometry, but completes it with smooth lines and adds extra geometric features to make it more unique and distinct.
unageo.story1: Over the years, I have used many different fonts for my projects and sometimes I thought that to better match my style, I could try to make my own typeface. I decided to give it a shot, even though I knew almost nothing about font creation itsef. I only knew that I would like my font to be geometric because that's my preferred style.
unageo.story2: I decided to work on the typeface with an unusual workflow. I made the characters in Inkscape, which I'm familiar with. Then I imported the outlines into FontForge, which I only tried for the first time. The process didn't take as long as I expected, and everything was done in a few days. I made each glyph in light and Black variant, made sure they were interpolable and then I adjusted the metrics and added kerning.
unageo.story3: Of course, I ran into some issues along the way and learned that fonts are more complicated than they look like. After I had everything figured out, I used Fontmake to generate a variable fonts and Fonttools to create static instances. There is still a lot I can learn, especially if I decide to make another font, and I'm sure this one isn't perfect either, so if you have an idea for an improvement, don't hesitate to submit a new issue on GitHub, and I'll take a look at it. See further down below.
unageo.ost:
Unageo is an open source typeface developed on GitHub.
If you have an idea for an improvement, bug to report or any other comment/suggestion, feel free to submit a new issue on GitHub.
Latest relase as well as the bleeding edge version is always available on GitHub along with the source files.
Typeface was recently accepted into Google Fonts and should be available in 2026 Q2.

wordgrind.about: WordGrind (言葉作業ゲー) is a simple web app for word memorization. It works by randomly picking a word from a deck and asking for the answer. Besides words and their answers it also features "back sides" (made for english meaning of kanji words) and hints, which can all be fully customized. It's a project that I primarily made for my personal use, however, you can also download it from GitHub and use it freely if you want.

opucestauprchlika.about:
The goal of this project was to transform a paper-based story game by OPU (Organizace pro pomoc uprchlíkům) about the journey of an Ukrainian family fleeing the war into a digital format. Its main purpose is to educate about the challenges these families face, with a particular focus on educating middle school students.
My Role in the Project
I was responsible for designing the game's interface and developing a high-fidelity clickable prototype using Figma, while following the organization's existing visual identity guidelines. In addition, I worked on shortening the texts, to enhance the game's appeal and ensure it fits on smaller screens.
